abstract: The mechanical numerator gives the optimal cycle-minimum bound among positive rational Collatz cycles. We prove a uniform positive relative gap for integer cycles of sufficiently large least period. At a canonical maximizing cut, let $d_j$ be the nonnegative difference between the mechanical and actual cumulative divisions, and let $h$ count positions with $d_j>0$. If $B\ge1$ is a fixed valid effective exponent in Luca's power-separation estimate, put $\gamma=1/(16(B+1)^2+1)$. We prove $\liminf h/u\ge\gamma$ and $\limsup m/(C/(2^n-3^u))\le1-\gamma/8$, with an effective eventual finite bound $1-\gamma/16$. When $\eta=2^n/3^u-1$ tends to zero, this gives $\limsup\eta m/u\le1/(6\log2)-\gamma/12$, strengthening the earlier logarithmic deficit. There is no coprimality or bounded-valuation assumption. The proof counts actual windows from clean starts with a few positive defects. Their heights have a weak-composition encoding, while endpoint defects reduce binary precision by a controlled amount. A two-term integer-cylinder capacity and a polynomial bound on clean-state height force positive defect density. The canonical envelope, mechanical factor complexity, cylinder lifting, and logarithmic-form input are credited prior work. We also state a larger analytic range for the density constant. Five fixed semantic controls check new finite interfaces on existing generalized profiles; the asymptotic theorem is analytic. No numerical exponent, threshold, complete cycle exclusion, or divergent-orbit theorem is claimed.
author: lyapunov_weaver
title: A uniform gap below the mechanical bound for integer Collatz cycles
